Many farmers and ranchers in eastern Colorado are curious about artificial intelligence, but they don’t have a local tech-savvy person to show them how to use it. Xue “Alice” Dong has made that her job. Dong, an IEEE senior member, is an extension regional specialist with the Colorado State University Extension , CSU’s outreach arm. She works in Logan County and serves a 10-county farming area in Colorado’s northeast corner. Her job is to turn university research into practical help for the people who live there. Xue “Alice” Dong Employer Colorado State University Extension in Logan County Title Extension regional specialist Member grade Senior member Alma maters Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot; Beijing Normal University; State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse; Colorado State University Global She built the AI-Powered Agritourism Chatbot (AgriTourismAI.com), which helps farmers and ranchers launch and run “agritourism” businesses. Agritourism is when farmers open their property to visitors for fun, education, or shopping events. Familiar examples include pick-your-own fruit orchards, lessons on how to grow vegetables, and sales of handmade products. Dong also teaches workshops where she shows farmers and ranchers how they can use AI tools to help grow and manage their business. She says she sees herself as a link between the university and the countryside. “We [extension specialists] act as a bridge,” she says. “We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Many farmers and ranchers are older, and they typically have no technical training. Often their children and grandchildren have left the farm to work in a city or otherwise aren’t around to teach them about new tools. Without help, the benefits of AI could pass the farmers by. Dong’s workshops give them a way in. Dong was named a finalist in the 2026 GenAI for Good Challenge for her AgriPivot AI Agent. The challenge was organized by IEEE Humanitarian Technologies and the U.N.’s International Telecommunication Union , and her project was selected from 318 teams across 79 countries. She also won the 2026 Award for Innovation from the National Extension Technology Community (NETC) , and both the 2025 national and Western regional Educational Technology Awards from the National Association of Community Development Extension Professionals (NACDEP). She has secured seven competitive grants totaling more than US $250,000 as principal investigator or co-principal investigator, including funding supported by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture . An early love of design and problem-solving Dong was born in Beijing. Both her parents are doctors. As a child, she liked drawing new and inventive things. Sketching, she says, lets her picture solutions to problems in her head and put them on paper as practical designs. That habit grew into a way of relating to her surroundings. “I’ve always had a passion to create something tangible that can solve problems in the real world,” she says. She doesn’t credit a single mentor for the direction her life has taken. Instead, she says all her teachers helped lay the groundwork for her career. She attended the Inner Mongolia Normal University , in Hohhot, an institution that trains teachers. She earned two bachelor’s degrees there in 2013—one in geographical science and one in education. She then earned a master’s degree in curriculum and instruction from Beijing Normal University in 2016. That year, she moved to the United States to continue her graduate studies at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry , in Syracuse. She earned a master’s degree in environmental biology in 2020. From outreach to extension work After earning her second master’s degree, she joined Paul Smith’s College , in Paul Smiths, N.Y., as an education and outreach coordinator. She managed several national watershed projects to protect rivers, lakes, and aquifers. Watersheds are areas of land from which water drains into bodies of water. She also undertook invasive-species-prevention projects, wrote grants to secure project funding, and designed two educational websites and several outreach publications. One website, Maintain the Chain , helps lake residents, boaters, and visitors from around the world keep invasive species out of the Fulton Chain of Lakes in New York’s Adirondack Park. In 2022, she joined Stewards of the Coast and Redwoods as program manager. The nonprofit, based in Guerneville, Calif., works with California State Parks to protect, restore, and educate the public about the parks along Sonoma County ’s coast and the Russian River area. The region is known for its redwood forests, wineries, and resort towns. She left in 2023 to join the CSU Extension as a regional specialist, a title she still holds. Her employer is part of the Cooperative Extension System , a nationwide network run by land-grant universities , schools founded with federal grants to teach farming and other practical subjects. Extension faculty and staff share what researchers at their universities learn with the citizens of those states. The cooperative system operates on three levels. It is overseen federally by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture , managed statewide through land-grant universities, and delivered locally by county offices and Extension agents across more than 3,000 counties. The work goes well beyond farming, Dong says, also covering community and economic development, health initiatives, and the 4-H program , which teaches children hands-on skills in agriculture, science, leadership, and citizenship. Extension faculty members’ performance is judged on their research, teaching, and service to the community, Dong says—similar to the way professors in academia are evaluated. The difference, she says, is the audience: Professors teach students; most extension specialists teach adults, including farmers, ranchers, and community leaders. The setting is different, too. Dong doesn’t commute from the campus to the countryside; she lives and works in it. Her office is in Sterling, a small rural town. But her projects serve the whole state, and many of the people she helps live one to four hours’ drive away. So, most of her work with farmers and ranchers happens by email, phone, and virtual meetings. County fairs, farmers markets, and agricultural events give her chances to meet large groups of them in person. She can’t just hand Colorado residents research findings and expect them to figure out the information they need, she says. “We need to translate that research into something more practical, and easier to use, that farmers and ranchers can understand immediately,” she says. Dong also focuses not on only on whether people use AI, but also on how they use it. In 2026, she and Paul Hill from Utah State University Extension published “From Access to Governance: Generative AI Literacy for Extension Professionals and Small Businesses, and a Governance-Aware Design Framework” in the journal AI . The paper offers a framework for helping Extension professionals and small businesses adopt generative AI responsibly. How her AI chatbot helps farmers and ranchers In 2025, Dong earned a third master’s degree , in artificial intelligence and machine learning, from CSU Global . She immediately put those skills to work on agritourism, she says. She built the chatbot in Python , a popular programming language . It answers typed questions, and its user interface looks much like ChatGPT ’s, but it works differently. Under the hood, it uses retrieval-augmented generation, a technique that has the AI look up information in a set of trusted documents before it answers. Dong curated that collection from Extension publications, so the chatbot’s answers rest on authoritative sources and are less likely to be made up. She presented the project at NeurIPS 2025 (Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems). The code is openly available on GitHub, so other Extension offices can adapt it. The bot runs in a web browser rather than as a phone app. Many farmers she works with don’t own a smartphone, Dong says, but nearly all have a computer, tablet, or other gadget that can connect to a website. The bot works on any of them, with no app to download. Extension specialists “act as a bridge. We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Farmers often ask the bot how to attract visitors and how to write a business plan. A farmer thinking about opening a corn maze, for example, can ask how to price admission, what kind of insurance to carry, and which permits to get. The bot also gives advice on managing risk. One of her test sites was Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch , in eastern Colorado. Dong documented how the ranch put AI to work in a peer-reviewed case study, “Revolutionizing Agritourism with AI and Machine Learning: A Case Study of Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch in Colorado,” published in 2025 in CABI Tourism Cases . Surveys and interviews she conducted with other users showed that people find it’s easy to use the bot, learn from it, and act on its advice, she says. She is preparing the full results for publication. Her work extends beyond agritourism. In 2026, she contributed an AI assistant to Project Pythia, an open-science program funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation and led by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) . The AI assistant turns raw airport weather report data into plain-language guidance for farmers and other non-technical users, and it tells users when data is missing rather than guessing. She also teaches workshops on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude , and Gemini . She has taught her workshop 20 times to more than 200 entrepreneurs and business owners, who came from 32 Colorado counties. In follow-up surveys, 90 percent of participants reported trying at least one new AI task in their business. Some of the workshops take place at a community center run by the Logan County Economic Development Corp ., in Sterling. She has also co-hosted the workshops with the Rural Community Assistance Corp ., Colorado Startup Week , and Boulder Startup Week . And she occasionally presents them as webinars, so people don’t have to travel. Her outreach has taught her that many farmers are eager to try new tools , she says. She shows them how simple her chatbot is to use. She also offers advice to high school students drawn to the field. Extension specialists each have a specialty, such as livestock, natural resources, food systems, or 4-H. Students should pick one based on their passion, she says. Land-grant universities offer related programs at the bachelor’s and master’s levels. For graduate students, she adds, Extension offers a third career path beyond academia and industry: “You apply advanced skills directly to the communities that need them.” How IEEE membership supports her career Dong joined IEEE in 2025 and soon was elevated to senior member. Her professional home is the IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology . She also serves as vice treasurer of the IEEE Denver Section’s Young Professionals group . IEEE supports all three parts of her job, she says. For research, she presented “Entrepreneur AI Agent: Empowering Small Businesses and Bridging the Digital Divide through Context-Aware Generative AI” at the 2026 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC). For teaching, she has offered to bring her AI workshop to Denver Section members and local entrepreneurs. For service, she reviews papers for IEEE conferences. IEEE conferences matter most to her, she says: “Through them, I can present my research and network with other researchers in the field.” She attended the IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology in Boulder, Colo., in September 2026. The event, she says, opened her eyes to many new projects underway across IEEE. Still, she says, her work always points back to the farms and ranches of eastern Colorado. Its people are curious, she says, but they can’t make the leap to new technology alone. “They really need this kind of a bridge,” she says.

“The people in the field are closest to the problem, closest to the situation, therefore that is where real wisdom is.” Colin Powell made this observation in 2001 to State Department staff upon becoming U.S. Secretary of State, emphasizing the importance of headquarters supporting overseas missions.
A quarter century later, Powell’s words still hold true and, while in a different setting, apply to Japan’s defense attaches: the Self-Defense Forces (SDF) officers stationed at embassies who gather military intelligence and liaise with host-country armed forces. Indeed, as Japan’s defense equipment and technology cooperation expands, their role is becoming increasingly important.
Since adopting the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology in 2014, Japan has accumulated experience in equipment transfers and international joint development. The abolition in April of five restrictions limiting arms exports to specific purposes — rescue, transport, warning, surveillance and minesweeping — is expected to strengthen the deterrence and response capabilities of allies and like-minded partners while safeguarding Japan’s domestic production capacity.

summary: 澳大利亚批评美国国会预算办公室 AUKUS 言论澳大利亚《海峡时报》批评美国国会预算办公室对 AUKUS 的评论 立即注册：深入了解亚洲快速发展的情况 澳大利亚国防部长理查德·马尔斯 (Richard Marles) 并不担心这份报告，“因为 AUKUS 正在发生”。发表于 2026 年 11 月 22 日上午 08:37 更新于 2026 年 11 月 22 日下午 12:50 澳大利亚国防部长理查德·马勒斯表示，美国国会预算办公室声称 AUKUS 将减少美国攻击潜艇的说法是“错误的”。 AUKUS将把弗吉尼亚级潜艇带到澳大利亚

发表于 2026 年 11 月 22 日 08:37
更新于 2026 年 11 月 22 日 12:50
澳大利亚国防部长理查德·马尔斯表示，美国国会预算办公室声称 AUKUS 将减少美国攻击潜艇的说法是“错误的”。
AUKUS将从2027年起将弗吉尼亚级潜艇引入澳大利亚，并于2030年左右开始销售，并推出新的英澳级潜艇。
堪培拉已承诺在 30 年内拨款 3680 亿澳元，而中国则称 AUKUS 危险，并警告称这可能会加剧军备竞赛。
悉尼——11月22日，澳大利亚国防部长理查德·马勒斯批评美国国会预算办公室（CBO）的一份报告称AUKUS协议将减少美国海军可用的攻击潜艇数量。
“他们错了，”马勒斯说，他指的是国会预算办公室，该机构在 11 月份的报告中表示，向澳大利亚出售弗吉尼亚级潜艇可能会在 2060 年之前缩小美国海军攻击潜艇部队的规模。
AUKUS是澳大利亚有史以来最大的国防项目，将从2027年开始在澳大利亚部署美国指挥的弗吉尼亚级潜艇，包括从2030年左右开始向澳大利亚出售几艘弗吉尼亚级潜艇，并将让英国和澳大利亚建造新型AUKUS核动力潜艇。
马尔斯在电视讲话中表示，他并不担心这份报告，“因为 AUKUS 正在发生”，而且“美国的生产率绝对在增加”。
10 月，Marles 表示，澳大利亚仍有望在 2030 年代初从美国购买第一艘核动力潜艇。
国会预算办公室没有立即回应正常工作时间之外的置评请求。
堪培拉已承诺在三十年内向 AUKUS 提供 3,680 亿澳元（3,140 亿新元），其中包括对英国和美国生产基地的数十亿美元投资。
AUKUS 成立于 2021 年，是对抗中国在印太地区日益增长的影响力的一部分。
中国称该协议很危险，并警告称它可能会引发地区军备竞赛。路透社

Published Nov 22, 2026, 08:37 AM

Australia’s Defence Minister Richard Marles said the US Congressional Budget Office was “wrong” to claim AUKUS would reduce US attack submarines.
AUKUS will bring Virginia-class submarines to Australia from 2027, with sales from around 2030 and a new UK-Australia submarine class.
Canberra has committed A$368 billion over 30 years, while China calls AUKUS dangerous and warns it could fuel an arms race.
SYDNEY – Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles on Nov 22 criticised the United States Congressional Budget Office (CBO) over a report that said the AUKUS pact would decrease the number of attack submarines available to the US Navy.
“They are wrong,” Marles said, referring to the CBO, which said in the report in November that the sale of Virginia-class submarines to Australia could diminish the size of the US Navy’s attack submarine force until 2060.
AUKUS, Australia’s largest-ever defence project, which will put US-commanded Virginia-class submarines in Australia from 2027, involves selling several Virginia-class submarines to Australia from around 2030 and will have Britain and Australia build a new class of AUKUS nuclear-powered submarine.
Marles was not worried about the report “because AUKUS is very much happening” and “the production rate in the United States is absolutely increasing”, he said in televised remarks.
In October, Marles said Australia remained on track ​to acquire its first ​nuclear-powered submarines from the US in the early 2030s.
The CBO did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside regular business hours.
Canberra has committed A$368 billion (S$314 billion) over three decades to AUKUS, including billions of dollars in investment in British and US production bases.
Formed in 2021, AUKUS is part of efforts to counter China’s growing influence in the Indo-Pacific.
China has called the pact dangerous and warned it could spur a regional arms race. REUTERS

content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和中国国家主席习近平一致认为，即使两国争夺人工智能霸主地位，人类也应该始终参与使用人工智能技术的军事决策，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特周五表示。特朗普在中国深圳与习近平会面归来后，贝森特对 CNBC 表示，该协议是特朗普亚洲之行的主要成果之一。贝森特表示：“我认为，特朗普总统和习主席一致认为，人类应该始终参与情报情报机构做出的任何军事决策，并且不应允许情报情报机构在重大军事行动中自主行事，这一点非常重要。”贝森特指的是特朗普政府对该技术的首选术语“超级智能”。贝森特表示，美中就该技术的军事使用达成的协议需要人类参与和其他保障措施，不会受到两国人工智能霸主竞争的影响。他补充说，美国人工智能实验室需要保持其技术领先地位，作为抵御网络攻击中使用的“危险”中国人工智能模型的最佳防御手段。贝森特说：“但是，当双方都同意不应该在无人参与的情况下发起任何重大军事行动时，这与竞争无关。”
他表示，涉及英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋和一名与他有恋情的中国公民的间谍指控并未在特习双边会晤中提及。贝森特表示，在特朗普采取他所谓的“非常强硬的路线”后，英伟达的第二级人工智能芯片 H200 仍然是中国可以通过许可购买的最先进的芯片。 “我认为我们看到的是中国人在 H200 上的订单很少，因为他们试图构建自己的芯片堆栈，而且我认为他们可能落后了很多年，”他补充道。英伟达丑闻发生后，贝森特淡化了财政部长和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克在人工智能芯片限制问题上所表达的分歧，称特朗普政府官员“都致力于遵循特朗普总统的指示”。美国商务部周一采取措施，进一步限制中国获得先进人工智能芯片，包括中国实体可以租用计算能力的海外数据中心使用的芯片。 “我认为我们将会看到适当的芯片限制已经到位，并且远程访问已经被限制，”他说。

【原文 English Original】
President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed humans should always be involved in military decisions that use artificial intelligence technologies, even as the two countries compete for AI supremacy , Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday. Bessent told CNBC after returning from Trump’s meeting with Xi in Shenzhen, China, that the agreement was among the major achievements of Trump’s trip to Asia. “I think it was very important that President Trump and President Xi agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions,” Bessent said, referring to the Trump administration’s preferred term for the technology, “super intelligence.” Bessent said that the U.S.-China agreement on military use of the technology, requiring human involvement and other safeguards, would not be affected by the two countries’ competition for AI supremacy. He added that U.S. AI labs needed to maintain their technological lead as the best defense against “dangerous” Chinese AI models that are being used in cyberattacks. “But there’s nothing to do with competition when it says that both sides agree that no major military operation should be launched without a human being involved,” Bessent said. He said that the spying allegations involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a Chinese national that he was romantically involved with did not come up in the Trump-Xi bilateral meeting. Bessent said that Nvidia’s second-tier AI chip, the H200, remained the most advanced chip that China could purchase with licenses, after Trump took what he called a “very firm line.” “I think what we have seen is a paucity of orders from the Chinese on the H200s as they try to build out their own chip stack, and I think that they are probably many years behind,” he added. Bessent downplayed differences that he had voiced between the views of Treasury and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on AI chip restrictions in the wake of the Nvidia scandal, saying Trump administration officials were “all committed to following President Trump’s instructions.” The Commerce Department took steps on Monday to further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips, including those used by overseas data centers where Chinese entities can rent computing power. “I think we are going to see that the proper chip restrictions are in place, and the remote access has been curtailed,” he said.

圖為2015年6月26日，一名投資者在安徽省阜陽市證券交易所大廳觀察股市。（VCG/VCG via Getty Images）
【大紀元2026年11月22日訊】（大紀元記者方曉報導）中國股市持續走弱之際，中共中央機關報《人民日報》11月21日刊文，稱唱空中國經濟者終會落空，批評境外媒體和機構炒作中國經濟危機、通縮及產能過剩等議題。然而，文章發表當天，中國網絡隨即出現大量嘲諷聲音，有網民反問：「不是唱空的問題，是唱的都沒了。」也有人表示，投資者正在經歷「人生中最大的財富縮水」，質疑官方喊話與股民實際處境之間的落差。
官媒題為「唱空中國經濟者終會落空」的文章宣稱，今年以來，一些境外媒體和機構頻頻唱空中國，炒作「通縮陷阱」、「中國衝擊2.0」、「中國經濟危機外溢」等說法，並以「產能過剩」指責中國製造業，試圖藉「中國崩潰」動搖外界信心。
文章認為，相關論調存在以偏概全、偷換概念等問題：中國經濟增速放緩，就被指增長模式難以為繼；經濟保持成長，又被說成依賴政策刺激；出口遇到壓力，就質疑中國製造競爭力；出口表現強勁，又被歸咎於產能過剩和內需不足。文章形容，這些說法無論中國經濟如何發展，都能得出負面結論。
但文章也承認，中國房地產市場承壓仍在調整，「供強需弱」使居民消費信心有待提振、新舊動能轉換速度不匹配、產業轉型升級「還有不少硬骨頭要啃」。
官媒上述文章發表之際，A股正經歷連日調整。中國三大股指11月20日全線下跌，上證綜合指數收報3533.79點，下跌1.22%，盤中最低觸及3500.83點，幾度逼近3500點關口；深證成指下跌3.09%，創業板指下跌3.54%，全市場超過5200隻股票下跌。
「唱空中國經濟者終會落空」隨後登上中國網絡熱搜榜。不少中國網友及財經自媒體人紛紛對這篇文章進行嘲諷。
有人說，「（中國）股市是自己空的，沒人唱空」，有人表示「不是唱空的問題，是唱的都沒了」。還有人指「那就漲起來讓做空中國的人全破產」。
更多網友直指，有投資人正經歷「人生中最大的財富縮水...人民日報，你要我怎麼相信你」。
微博會員「斯庫里」發貼說，假如哪天中國經濟真的面臨徹底完蛋的話，你們以為我們不會出去「搶」嗎？ ​
微博會員「小豬搞機」嘲諷道：雖說外媒在唱空，但中國A股也不爭氣啊！我上週虧了40%，肉疼的我…… ​
包括微博會員「留得青山等風起」在內的多名網友揶揄：《人民日報》別打嘴炮，下星期就讓做空中國股市的人虧破產行嗎？！股市就是臉面，股市就是人心！
中共國家統計局11月16日公布的10月經濟數據，10月規模以上工業增加值年增4.8%，低於市場預期的5.3%；社會消費品零售總額年增0.4%，低於9月的1.1%，也不及市場預期的0.8%。
投資數據同樣疲弱。今年1至10月，全國固定資產投資（不含農戶）年減8.1%，其中房地產開發投資下降21.6%；同期新建商品房銷售面積下降13.7%，銷售額下降14.3%。
官媒強調外界唱空論調不可信，但股市下跌、消費增長放緩及房地產持續調整，仍是民眾切身感受到的經濟壓力。這也是《人民日報》文章登上熱搜後，網民反應與官方論述形成反差的背景。

title: The military lacks an ‘overarching plan’ to improve munition stockpiles—partly because it’s no one’s job
zh_title: 军方缺乏改善弹药库存的“总体计划”——部分原因是这不是任何人的工作
summary: 根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军队可以购买的东西和实际需要的东西之间的差异。
content:
根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军方可以购买的东西与实际需要的东西之间存在差异，政府问责局表示，这甚至可能导致弹药投资超出五角大楼的要求。该报告的作者写道：“虽然国防部正在采取措施关注弹药短缺问题，但它无法解决这些差距。” “国防部没有总体计划，也没有指定和授权的领导层来改善弹药库存并满足其弹药需求。由于没有确定长期目标、实现这些目标的战略以及衡量进展的指标，国防部无法确定其行动是否能够解决弹药短缺问题。”包括国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯在内的高级政府官员否认美国存在弹药短缺，尽管有报告和独立分析显示，伊朗冲突已经严重耗尽了弹药。关键武器，尤其是备受追捧的爱国者拦截机，其制造时间可能超过两年。
但在对政府问责局研究的回应中，五角大楼官员同意军方需要制定一项长期计划来提高弹药生产的建议。五角大楼负责采购的代理副手大卫·卡德曼写道：“我们同意需要一个总体框架，更好地整合弹药需求、库存水平、生产、资源和长期目标。”他补充说，国防部“已经执行了政府问责局建议中的许多内容”。美国政府问责局的研究并未探讨特定弹药的库存，而是研究了五角大楼跟踪、预测和总体处理一系列武器（从炮弹到战斧导弹）的过程。 “重要的是，[这项研究]与当前的短缺无关，”战略与国际研究中心的高级顾问马克·坎西恩（Mark Cancian）撰写了大量有关弹药政策的文章。 “这关系到未来并决定长期库存、生产和弹药组合。”  国防官员强调需要“高低”弹药组合，即高科技、难以制造的武器和廉价武器之间的平衡。伊朗战争说明了美军对昂贵拦截机的依赖，这些拦截机投入了大量资金来击落廉价的沙赫德无人机，这些无人机的成本只有数万美元。
彭博资讯国防分析师韦恩·桑德斯表示：“当你拥有先进的能力，并且开始消耗先进的能力来击落快速补充的非先进能力时，这是一场我们赢不了的经济游戏。”“这开始转变为军事领域的一场革命，表明我们必须改变我们的学说，同时改变我们在美国的生产能力。”   美国政府问责局国防能力主管戴安娜·摩尔达夫斯基 (Diana Moldafsky) 在周五发给《防务一号》的一封电子邮件中指出，五角大楼已经发现了不足之处

The Defense Department has no “overarching plan” to identify, achieve, or measure its progress toward long-term munition production goals, according to a Government Accountability Office study released on Thursday, which said the military was too reactive to global events and unprepared to forecast its own needs. The GAO cited—among other issues—a lack of centralized authority over weapons inventories, which have been depleted by the Iran war and are vital to U.S. plans for a potential conflict with China. At the center of the problem lies a discrepancy between what the military can buy and what it actually needs, which the GAO said could even result in munition investments that exceed the Pentagon’s requirements.  “While DOD is taking steps to focus on munitions shortages, it is not positioned to address these gaps,” the report’s authors wrote. “DOD does not have an overarching plan or designated and empowered leadership to improve munition inventories and meet its munitions requirements. By not identifying long-term goals, strategies to achieve them, and metrics to gauge progress, DOD cannot be sure that its actions will address its munition shortfalls. ” Top administration officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, have denied that the U.S. has a shortage in munitions, despite reports and independent analyses showing the Iran conflict has alarmingly drained key weapons, especially for highly-sought Patriot interceptors that can take more than two years to make. But in its response to the GAO study, Pentagon officials concurred with the recommendation that the military needed to develop a long-term plan to improve its munition production.  “We agree with the need for an overarching framework that better integrates munition requirements, inventory levels, production, resources, and long-term objectives,” wrote David Cadman, the Pentagon’s acting deputy for acquisitions, who added that the department “already executes many elements” of the GAO’s recommendation. The GAO study did not explore the inventories of specific munitions, but examined the processes by which an expansive list of weapons — from artillery shells to Tomahawk missiles — are tracked, forecast and generally addressed by the Pentagon. “The important thing is that [the study] is not about current shortages,” Mark Cancian, a senior adviser with the Center for Strategic and International Studies who has written extensively on munitions policy. “It's about the future and deciding long-term inventories, production, and munitions mixes.”  Defense officials have emphasized the need for a “high-low” mix of munitions—that is, a balance between high-tech, hard-to-make weapons and cheaper ones. The Iran war illustrated the U.S. military’s reliance on expensive interceptors, which were heavily expended to shoot down cheap Shahed drones that only cost tens of thousands of dollars.  “When you have an exquisite capacity, and you are starting to expend an exquisite capacity to knock down non-exquisite capabilities that are rapidly replenished, it is an economical game that we're not going to win,” said Wayne Sanders, a defense analyst with Bloomberg Intelligence. “This is starting to turn into one of those revolutions in military affairs to say we have to change our doctrine as well as we change our production capacity in the U.S.”   In an email to Defense One on Friday, the GAO’s director for defense capabilities, Diana Moldafsky, noted that the Pentagon had identified shortfalls before the conflict with Iran, but said that the war “made addressing those shortages more urgent.” “Our key point is that meeting DOD's munitions requirements will be challenging,” Moldafsky said. “A department-wide plan would help the department direct its resources towards its most critical munitions needs.”  Cancian said that Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and the consequent transfer of Patriots and other weapons to Kyiv, introduced concerns about the defense industrial base and its ability to respond to munition needs around the world. Meanwhile, the Pentagon has inked billions of dollars in multi-year “framework agreements” with top defense companies over the last year to help increase high-tech munition production, which require funding from Congress to come to fruition. The Trump administration also invoked the Defense Production Act earlier this year in an attempt to bolster munition supply chains. A Pentagon spokesperson declined to address the GAO study directly, or even to be quoted by name. But they said the military is “fully equipped to strike at the time and place of the President’s choosing…while preserving a deep, ready stockpile to defend our people and interests.” Part of the problem is that no one authority is really in charge of keeping arsenals topped off and ready, the report found.  The GAO identified several Pentagon offices and working groups, including individual service entities, responsible for managing munition inventories, but no one dedicated authority “that empowers the leadership to make decisions that improve munitions inventories department-wide and hold them accountable for the outcomes achieved, such as improving munitions inventory levels.” The study also said that the services maintain separate tools to track munition inventories, which then feed into a Pentagon system known as the Munitions Readiness Initiative. But researchers said the DOD has limited oversight over that tracking platform and hasn’t regularly reconciled it with service-level numbers. Citing an unnamed Pentagon official in its acquisitions and sustainment office, the GAO said “the office was reluctant to impose additional responsibilities on the services for maintaining data to meet MRI’s needs because they recognize that the services already face numerous responsibilities in managing their own munitions inventory data.” The Pentagon concurred with most of the GAO’s recommendations, but only partially agreed with one: that the data management plan be run out of the DOD’s digital and AI office. Cadman’s response said that the Pentagon’s acquisition and sustainment arm was best suited to develop it. ]]>

Satellite imagery has revealed an unusual uncrewed aircraft at Pucheng, China, with a configuration that bears very strong similarities to Boeing’s carrier-based MQ-25 Stingray . While we still have no idea about the function of the drone, the facility itself also appears to be an increasingly important hub for China’s expanding uncrewed aircraft industry . A wider-view satellite image provided to TWZ by Vantor shows the mystery drone at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor The drone initially attracted attention after being spotted in a satellite image of Pucheng Neifu Airport in Shaanxi Province, in northwestern China, available through Apple Maps. A separate image of the drone, where it appears on a runway, is also available through Bing Maps. TWZ subsequently obtained imagery of Pucheng from Vantor showing the uncrewed aircraft in question. what a suprise! Three UAV spotted at Pucheng on apple maps. CH-7, Jiutian and a MQ-25 like UAV. pic.twitter.com/rREqLuFAdU — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) November 18, 2026 spotted again on bing maps! and it's on the runway this time pic.twitter.com/xLgZetmOZf — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) November 19, 2026 As well as the unidentified aircraft, imagery from Pucheng dating from April of this year also reveals what appears to be a CH-7 stealthy flying-wing drone and an example of the heavyweight jet-powered Jiutian mothership drone . A CH-7 at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor A Jiutian drone mothership at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor The most obvious comparison for the unidentified aircraft is Boeing’s MQ-25 Stingray. The MQ-25 is a carrier-based uncrewed aircraft developed primarily to provide aerial refueling for U.S. Navy aircraft, extending the range and operational flexibility of carrier air wings. It also provides a foundation for future uncrewed naval aviation capabilities . In terms of dimensions, the unidentified Chinese UAV has a wingspan of approximately 66 feet and a length of 49 feet, according to Vantor. In contrast, the MQ-25 measures approximately 75 feet in wingspan and 51 feet in length. MQ-25 Stingray. Boeing The Chinese drone appears to occupy a similar general design category, but there are several important differences notable at this stage. One of the most noticeable is the forward fuselage. Unlike the MQ-25, whose forward section has a relatively flattened, shovel-like appearance, the Chinese aircraft appears to have a more conventional, tapered nose. Perhaps this could incorporate a conical radome housing radar equipment. That theory, and it is just a theory, could be supported by the different color of the nose compared to the yellow primer-painted airframe. The air intake is also different. Rather than the exotic, flush inlet associated with the MQ-25 , the Chinese design has a more conventional dorsal intake that appears serrated to help with radar signature and/or split into two channels. Another possibility is that the aircraft has two engines, although that remains speculative, based on the apparent bifurcated intake. A side-by-side look at the drone seen in the image of Pucheng, at left, and an MQ-25, offering comparative views of their inlets. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor/Boeing The tail configuration may also be distinctive, with a laterally flared V-tail, like the MQ-25, but possibly incorporating visible control surfaces instead of an all-moving tailplane design. Taken together, these features suggest an aircraft that shares some of the MQ-25’s general design philosophy but is not an attempt at a direct clone. Long-time Chinese aerospace observer and TWZ contributor Andreas Rupprecht , who has been following developments surrounding the aircraft, believes China could be following a development path similar to Boeing’s, potentially producing a carrier-based uncrewed aerial refueling platform that can also undertake intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions. “I think China is actually following the same path as Boeing here, and it’s heading towards a tanker that can also take on other roles as an ISR platform,” Rupprecht told us. A radar-equipped aircraft with substantial endurance could potentially perform surveillance and other sensor-related missions when not being used as a tanker. The potential development of a multirole uncrewed tanker at Pucheng would also fit into a much broader push by China to expand the role of uncrewed aircraft in its naval aviation forces. One of the most notable developments is the GJ-21 , a navalized derivative of the GJ-11 Sharp Sword stealth uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV). Featuring folding wings and provisions for catapult launches and arrested recoveries, the low-observable flying-wing design is intended to operate from China’s growing fleet of large-deck warships , including the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan . In October 2026, Chinese state media reported that the GJ-21 had successfully completed its first takeoff and landing aboard the vessel, a significant milestone in the development of shipborne fixed-wing combat drones. GJ-21 carrier-based UCAV. via Chinese internet The GJ-21 effort is taking place alongside the introduction of China’s new catapult-equipped Fujian aircraft carrier, which has begun operating the J-35 stealth fighter, J-15T carrier-based fighter, and KJ-600 airborne early warning aircraft. Taken together, these developments point to an increasingly ambitious effort to integrate uncrewed aircraft into China’s future carrier air wings , potentially spanning stealthy strike platforms, surveillance systems, and other specialized support aircraft. The unidentified Pucheng aircraft could represent another, quite different part of that wider effort — or something else altogether. At the same time, this aircraft is roughly 20 percent dimensionally smaller than the MQ-25, which would mean it would have less fuel to give. It’s also worth noting that Boeing’s MQ-25 emerged from an unmanned combat air vehicle (UCAV) design that included low-observable features. Multirole UCAV concepts predating it also looked very similar. The MRE concept from Lockheed during the 1990s looks very similar to the MQ-25 we know today. (Lockheed Martin) In addition, Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), for instance, the FQ-42 Vengeance, and also the XQ-67 Off-Board Sensing Station share a similar overall design. With this in mind, and remembering its different nose section, this could just as easily be a true multirole UCAV or even a CCA, such as one designed for force protection of high-value aerial assets, and it may not even be carrier-capable. Rupprecht cautioned that the manufacturer of the mystery drone remains unidentified. However, one of the more interesting clues about the aircraft’s possible origins comes from Shenyang Aircraft Corporation (SAC). Rupprecht pointed to a propeller-driven demonstrator unveiled by SAC in 2025, which he believes could fit the development lineage of the larger aircraft now visible at Pucheng. The sub-scale propeller-driven demonstrator unveiled by SAC in 2025. The background reads (rough translation): “Rollout Ceremony for Final Assembly of Shenyang’s First ‘Surrogate Flight Test’ Pilot-Test Verification Platform UAV.” via Chinese internet A smaller, propeller-driven demonstrator could provide a relatively inexpensive way to investigate aerodynamic characteristics, autonomous flight controls, mission systems, and other technologies before progressing to a much larger aircraft. This piston-powered, propeller-driven aircraft with a broadly similar configuration to the MQ-25 was seen in a video flying, as well. 突然想起中国一家民营无人机公司，做过一款MQ-25活塞桨叶版 https://t.co/Y69dfzpLNS pic.twitter.com/IzU08PC8DK — 飞刀 (@chaoyinsukandao) November 18, 2026 Whether the Pucheng aircraft is related to this SAC demonstrator or if it’s an entirely separate program remains unknown. Beyond the external resemblance, there are no indications that they are linked, and the aircraft could just be a general test surrogate platform. The configuration isn’t totally novel in the advanced UAS world. The aircraft’s appearance is also interesting given the location where it has been spotted. Pucheng Neifu Airport is located in Shaanxi Province, and its surrounding aviation facilities include an area identified in Apple Maps as the National Aeronautics Industrial Base Pucheng General Aviation Industrial Park Guanliban. The industrial park has its own smaller runway, separate from the main airport infrastructure. A close-up of Pucheng with no drones visible, as of June 16, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 The site had remained relatively obscure to outside observers until roughly the past one to two years, according to Rupprecht. More recently, however, various aircraft manufacturers have apparently been conducting testing there. This raises the possibility that Pucheng is not simply an individual manufacturer’s flight-test location, but a facility used by multiple organizations developing and evaluating uncrewed aircraft. Rupprecht also raised the possibility that Pucheng could potentially be a specialized uncrewed aircraft testing facility associated with China’s Flight Test Establishment at Xi’an, commonly known as CFTE. “I cannot say (yet) whether this — and this is my theory — is effectively a branch of the CFTE at Xi’an, which is for crewed and this is a base for uncrewed ones,” Rupprecht explained. A satellite image provided to TWZ by Vantor provides an overview of Pucheng as of April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor If Pucheng does serve as a shared testing location for multiple manufacturers, it could help explain the appearance of several otherwise unrelated UAV designs at the same site. Returning to the mystery drone, the combination of its apparent size, configuration, and possible connection to earlier Chinese demonstrator programs makes it an interesting development to watch. Regardless, for now, the imagery from Pucheng offers a glimpse of a potentially significant new Chinese uncrewed aircraft program. summary: 印度海军已表示有兴趣支持开发旋转爆震发动机（RDE）驱动的超音速海军导弹。该问题陈述是在 2026 年 10 月举行的 Swavlamban 2026 海军旗舰展览期间发布的纲要的一部分，旨在展示国防创新。问题陈述的全文如下：该问题陈述确定了与旋转爆震发动机 (RDE) 研究相关的拟议本土超音速海军导弹计划。 RDE 研究将旋转爆炸作为推进原理。挑战
content:
印度海军已表示有兴趣支持开发旋转爆震发动机（RDE）驱动的超音速海军导弹。该问题陈述是在 2026 年 10 月举行的 Swavlamban 2026 海军旗舰展览期间发布的纲要的一部分，旨在展示国防创新。问题陈述的全文如下：该问题陈述确定了与旋转爆震发动机 (RDE) 研究相关的拟议本土超音速海军导弹计划。 RDE 研究将旋转爆炸作为推进原理。面临的挑战是确定它是否为所述海军应用提供可靠、可支持的能力途径。评估应区分科学可行性、组件成熟度、综合演示准备情况和服务使用资格。需要独立的证据来证实所声称的相对于现有推进替代方案的优势。该计划应在整个评估过程中保持明确的要求、配置控制、专家安全监督和结果的可追溯性。国内设计所有权、制造可重复性、环境适应性和长期支持是核心考虑因素。预期结果是对可行性和成熟度进行基于证据的评估，并得到授权研究和评估的支持。
在其他航空航天应用中取得的进展不应被视为海军导弹已做好准备的证明。燃气轮机和冲压发动机等传统发动机通过亚音速燃烧过程（也称为爆燃）产生推力。爆震发动机利用持续超音速燃烧（也称为爆震）产生的冲击波来产生推力。这意味着，对于相似的尺寸和重量等级，与燃气轮机或冲压发动机相比，爆震发动机不仅可以提供更大的推力，而且可以提供更高的效率。一家名为 D-Propulse Aerospace 的印度初创公司于 2026 年 7 月在 DRDO 测试设施测试了 RDE 原型机，在 24 小时内进行了五次静态测试。 D-Propulse 随后公布了开发 RDE 动力的吸气式超音速巡航导弹和旋转爆震火箭发动机 (RDRE) 动力的微型 SAM 的计划，用于反 UAS 应用。 《海军新闻》联系了创始人兼首席执行官 Saurav Jha，询问该公司对海军问题陈述的看法：D-Propulse 打算利用其吸气式 RDE 技术来制造超音速巡航导弹，这种导弹比传统系统更小、更便宜，但仍能达到作战射程。这将允许迄今为止只能承载距离更短的系统的平台进行承载。较低的价格点将使印度军方能够实现真正的大规模精确化。
毕竟，超音速巡航导弹比其他类型的系统到达目标的概率要高得多。因此，超音速巡航导弹的弹匣深度是当今情况下的关键要求，我们的目标价格点应该能够实现这一点。 D-Propulse 的马赫 3 超音速巡航导弹的 CAD 渲染图（图片来自 D-Propulse） 在回答有关与海军就 RDE 海军导弹进行谈判的问题时，Jha 表示，D-Propulse 一直在与相关利益相关者就其正在开发的系统进行磋商，包括通过既定机制寻求支持。在海德拉巴测试的发动机已在 Swavlamban 2026 上展出，是经过验证的发动机

【原文 English Original】
The Indian Navy has expressed interest in supporting the development of a Rotating Detonation Engine (RDE) – powered supersonic naval missile. The problem statement was part of a compendium released during Swavlamban 2026, the Navy’s flagship exhibition meant to showcase defence innovation, held in October 2026. The full text of the problem statement is as follows: This problem statement identifies a proposed indigenous supersonic naval missile programme associated with Rotating Detonation Engine (RDE) research. RDE research examines rotating detonation as a propulsion principle. The challenge is to establish whether it offers a credible, supportable capability pathway for the stated naval application. The assessment should distinguish scientific feasibility, component maturity, integrated demonstrator readiness and qualification for service use. Independent evidence is required to substantiate claimed advantages against established propulsion alternatives. The programme should maintain clear requirements, configuration control, specialist safety oversight and traceability of results throughout its evaluation. Domestic design ownership, manufacturing repeatability, environmental suitability and long-term support are central considerations. The expected outcome is an evidence-based assessment of feasibility and maturity, supported by authorised research and evaluation. Demonstrated progress in another aerospace application should not be treated as proof of readiness for a naval missile. Traditional engines like gas turbines and ramjets generate thrust by subsonic combustion process, also known as deflagration. Detonation engines utilize the shockwaves generated due to sustained supersonic combustion, also known as detonation, to generate thrust. This means that for a similar size and weight class, detonation engines can not only provide greater thrust but also better efficiency compared to gas turbines or ramjets. An Indian startup named D-Propulse Aerospace had tested an RDE prototype at a DRDO test facility in July 2026, conducting five static tests in 24 hours. D-Propulse subsequently unveiled plans to develop RDE powered air-breathing supersonic cruise missiles and rotating detonation rocket engine (RDRE) powered micro-SAMs for counter-UAS applications. Naval News reached out to founder and CEO Saurav Jha to inquire about the firm’s views regarding the Navy’s problem statement: D-Propulse intends to leverage its air-breathing RDE technology to build supersonic cruise missiles that are much smaller and cheaper than legacy systems and yet reach operational ranges. This would allow carriage by platforms that hitherto could only carry much shorter ranged systems. The lower price point will enable true mass in precision for the Indian military. After all, supersonic cruise missiles have a much higher probability of arrival over target than other types of systems out there. So, having magazine depth for supersonic cruise missiles is a key requirement in today’s scenario and our target price point should enable that. CAD Rendering of D-Propulse’s Mach 3 Supersonic Cruise Missile (Image via D-Propulse) In response to a question regarding talks with the Navy for the RDE naval missile, Jha stated that D-Propulse has been in consultation with the relevant stakeholders for the system it is developing, including for support through established mechanisms. The engine tested at Hyderabad was put on display at Swavlamban 2026 and is the proof motor of a flight-capable design. Naval News has learnt that based on that test data, new iterations will be fabricated and tested at the company’s newly constructed large connected-pipe Combustor Test Facility. D-Propulse aims to compress the developmental cycle significantly with this facility and has offered the facility to other small engine developers. Naval News also requested comments from Jha regarding the rationale behind the planned development of the RDRE micro-SAM: The idea behind the RDRE-powered micro SAM is to flip the economics of war in the favour of the defender. RDRE-powered micro-SAMs will be faster and more maneuverable than existing systems, allowing the user to address a wider range of incoming subsonic loitering munitions. Our studies show that RDRE technology can bring down the cost of effective systems greatly, perhaps even to the point of these being seen as ‘consumable ammunition’ if the production runs are large enough. And given the saturation scenarios we are seeing across conflict zones such as the Persian Gulf, where literally thousands of low-RCS subsonic munitions are being lobbed at air defence networks, I believe that our RDRE power counter UAS micro SAM will be required in very significant numbers in the near future. D-Propulse intends to offer the air-breathing RDE powered supersonic cruise missile for user trials by the end of 2029 and intends to offer the RDRE powered micro-SAM by mid-2028. Globally, extensive work is being done in the United States on developing RDE technology. Under the DARPA GAMBIT program, RTX’s Pratt & Whitney had completed a series of RDE tests in 2025. AFRL has also worked on RDE technology and recently expressed interest in combined-cycle RDRE , seeking a flight demonstration to validate the system’s operational viability. GE Aerospace had tested turbine- based combined-cycle RDE in 2023. In January 2026, Lockheed Martin and GE Aerospace demonstrated a liquid fuel RDE for missiles. Venus Aerospace , L3Harris and IN Space LLC are also developing various types of detonation engines. In the Indian context, an RDE powered supersonic missile would be complementary to the BrahMos . While the latter with its proven production run and ever increasing range will remain the mainstay weapon of the Navy, lighter subsonic and supersonic missiles are likely to proliferate due to cost and weight benefits. Missiles like the NASM-SR and NASM-MR are being developed by DRDO. The lighter form factor of an RDE powered naval missile may make it analogous to the BrahMos NG, which is currently in the R&D stage. Dr. Jaiteerth Joshi, CEO of BrahMos Aerospace, recently told ANI that the first model of BrahMos NG is expected by 2029. Once fabricated, several rounds of trials are required before the missile can be inducted. Dr. Joshi also confirmed the development of a 1,500 km ranged version of the BrahMos, up from the current maximum of about 800 km . The range extension will continue to occur in a phased manner and the 1,500 km range version has been designed and is currently undergoing simulations. BrahMos Aerospace has a nearly a full orderbook and continues to bag export orders. After ordering three batteries for $370 million in 2022 , the Philip p ines is reportedly exploring purchase of “at least six additional BrahMos batteries.” India has also offered to explore the integration of BrahMos on Philippine naval vessels. Five Akash SAM regiments and the Pinaka MLRS are also being looked at by the Philippine Marines and Army, Firstpost reported. Earlier, India’s defence secretary had confirmed that initial deals were signed with two more countries in Southeast Asia for the BrahMos. Vietnam is likely to receive a single coastal battery worth about $100 million while Indonesia has signed two $100 million contracts. Both countries are expected to place larger orders in the coming years. Philippine Marines showcase the BrahMos anti-ship missile system for the first time during the service’s 75th anniversary. More on Swavlamban 2026 Other notable firms with flagship projects present at Swavlamban 2026 included: Sagar Defence Engineering which developed the Matangi USV. Sagar Defence has commenced delivery of 12 meter class USVs to the Navy in 2026 after receiving an order for 12 USVs. Xinfinti Aerospace is developing Naval Chetak Autonomous System (NCAS). NCAS is supported by the Navy under iDEX program and seeks to convert HAL Chetak helicopters into uncrewed assets, an endeavor attempted and aborted by a HAL – IAI combine in the 2010s. Kalam Labs has obtained an iDEX contract from the Navy for the development of floating aircraft carriers. Co-founder Ahmed Faraaz told Naval News that the product will be an airship that can transport Kalam Labs’ suite of propeller driven high-altitude proven swarm-capable UAVs to altitudes exceeding 50,0000 feet. The altitude will enable the airship to stay protected from anti-aircraft munitions while conducting ISR and deploying UAVs for various tasks. Kalam Labs has deployed its UAVs from altitudes greater than 100,000 feet using balloons. Faraaz told Naval News that the firm has also bagged iDEX contracts from IAF for development of a supersonic autonomous spaceplane and mesh enabled space drone swarms. 【原文 English Original】
Following a week of busy launch activity, the worldwide launch manifest is set to see six launches this week, with three SpaceX Falcon 9 missions from Vandenberg, two Chinese missions, and an Ariane 6 mission from South America. SpaceX will launch payloads for the United States Space Force and the National Reconnaissance Office, while at least one of this week’s Chinese missions and the Ariane 6 will launch a batch of internet satellites. Chang Zheng 2D | Unknown Payload Wednesday, Nov. 18, will see a launch from China, with a Chang Zheng 2D (CZ-2D) expected to launch from Launch Complex 9 (LC-9) at the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center at 22:50 UTC. Official warning notices indicate a southerly launch trajectory, but details of the payload and its intended orbit will not be released until after launch. The two-stage, 40.77-m-tall CZ-2D is manufactured by the Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology (SAST). The 2D variant requires no additional strap-on boosters. This flight will mark the 108th CZ-2D to fly, the seventh of this year. Falcon 9 | USSF-317 (R-6) SpaceX’s first of two launches this week comes on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at the start of a four-hour launch window that opens at 7:00 PM PST (03:00 UTC on Thursday). The only mission for the United States Space Force (USSF) this week, the USSF-317 mission will launch from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) in California, flying southeast to place its classified payload into low-Earth orbit (LEO). All systems are looking good, and weather is favorable for liftoff. Propellant load is about to begin for Falcon 9’s launch of the USSF-627 mission from California → https://t.co/IdlZbviZZl pic.twitter.com/fKxyN4DIui — SpaceX (@SpaceX) November 12, 2026 Booster B1100 will support this mission, marking its eleventh flight since first supporting Starlink Group 11-30 nearly a year ago on Nov. 23, 2025. Eight of the booster’s previous flights supported Starlink missions, in addition to flying NROL-105 and USSF-385. SpaceX’s west coast droneship, Of Course I Still Love You, will be stationed downrange for B1100’s landing approximately eight minutes after liftoff. Falcon 9 is a 3.9-m-diameter, 70-m-tall two-stage rocket. Nine Merlin 1D engines power the first-stage booster, while the second stage uses a single vacuum-optimized Merlin engine. Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy were the first orbital rockets to achieve regular re-use, with one Falcon booster having flown 37 flights. The two payload fairings are also recovered and reused after flight. Chang Zheng 8A | SatNet LEO Group The second Chinese launch of the week is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, at 11:00 UTC from the Commercial LC-1 pad at the Wenchang Space Launch Site in China. A Chang Zheng 8A (CZ-8A) will carry nine communications satellites into LEO, with the satellites owned by SatNet and operated by the China Satellite Network Group. The CZ-8A rocket features two 3.35-m-diameter stages, with a total height of 50.54 m. The first stage is assisted by two strap-on liquid-fuelled boosters. This flight will mark the 13th overall CZ-8A flight, the seventh of 2026. Falcon 9 | NROL-136 SpaceX’s second Falcon 9 mission of the week is scheduled to launch on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 4:30 AM PST (12:30 UTC), again from SLC-4E at VSFB in California. The NROL-136 mission will carry an unknown number of payloads into LEO for the National Reconnaissance Office’s (NRO) Proliferated Architecture constellation, built by SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The booster supporting this mission will be B1097, flying for the 14th time. This booster first flew on Sept. 3, 2025, and has previously flown eight Starlink missions, as well as NROL-172, Transporter 17, Sentinel-6B, Twilight (Pandora & Others), and USSF-259. Following stage separation, B1097 will conduct a return-to-launch-site landing at Landing Zone 4 (LZ-4), located directly next to SLC-4E. Ariane 64 | Amazon Leo (LE-04) Amazon is continuing to put together its constellation of Leo satellites and will add another 36 on Monday, Nov. 23, at 10:12 UTC aboard an Ariane 64. The rocket will launch from Ensemble de Lancement Ariane 4 (ELA-4) at the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana, with the launch window lasting five hours and 27 minutes. Ariane 64 will follow a northeastern trajectory, delivering 22,000 kg of Leo satellites into LEO. Ariane 64 is a 62-m-tall, 5.4-m-diameter, expendable two-stage rocket built by the ArianeGroup on behalf of the European Space Agency. Both stages are powered by liquid hydrogen and oxygen-fuelled engines. The 64 variant of the basic Ariane 6 utilizes four P129 strap-on solid rocket boosters to provide additional lift-off thrust.
